title: DIET: Customized Slimming for Incompatible Networks in Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Edge-deployed recommender systems need to personalize models for specific devices while limiting on-edge computation, network transfers, bandwidth usage, and storage consumption.

gap.claim: Existing edge-specific fine-tuning methods require substantial on-edge computational resources and frequent network transfers to keep models up to date.

contributions.claim: DIET deploys a shared generic backbone across devices and generates edge-specific slimming subnets from past interactions for efficient personalization and transfer.
DIET incorporates inter-layer relationships when generating slimming subnets.
DIETING uses a single layer of parameters to represent an entire network for more storage-efficient deployment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DIET reduces inference time while obtaining more suitable diets.
The authors report that DIETING achieves comparably excellent performance with greater storage efficiency.
Experiments on four state-of-the-art datasets and two widely used models are reported to show superior recommendation accuracy and transmission and storage efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems are being deployed on mobile edges to reduce congestion from frequent mobile requests.
Prior methods fine-tune edge-specific models using nearby real-time data.
These methods impose computational, transfer, bandwidth, and user-satisfaction costs.
DIET shares a generic backbone and creates personalized slimming subnets for individual edges, while accounting for inter-layer relationships.
DIETING improves storage efficiency through shared parameter representation, and experiments report gains in accuracy and deployment efficiency.

source_observation.claim: A shared backbone can be personalized by generating device-specific subnets from interaction history.

interpretation.claim: Personalization can be separated from maintaining a fully distinct model on every edge.

application.claim: Consider subnet-level adaptation when deploying personalized models across heterogeneous edge devices.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves under device constraints or interaction histories outside the reported experiments.

source_observation.claim: Repeated network modules can be represented using a single parameter layer while retaining comparable performance.

interpretation.claim: Parameter sharing across repeated modules may reduce storage without necessarily sacrificing reported performance.

application.claim: Evaluate shared representations for repeated components in storage-constrained model deployments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which repeated modules are supported or the conditions under which performance remains comparable.

unknowns: Dataset names, model names, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The slimming-generation procedure and inter-layer relationship mechanism are not described.
Hardware settings and exact transmission, storage, inference-time, and accuracy measurements are not provided.
